liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Hollow** (1 review, 1 other source): Singled out as sounding great; Noted as the final Grateful Dead performance of this song [3][6]
- **Oh Boy** (2 reviews): Described as a rare public performance of this song; Attendee recalls it pulled out as an encore and being very sweet [5][14]
- **Friend Of The Devil** (1 review): Reviewer particularly loves this version [8]

## Setlist highlights

- **Oh Boy**: back after 211 archived shows (890 days); rare: 6 archived performances [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-04-25.sbd.gems.103640.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 9 songs; 38 min; rated 3.62/5 by 13 [1]
- **gd81-04-25.aud.munder.9728.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 9 songs; 38 min; rated 3.6/5 by 5 [2]. Said about its sound: Sounds more like a soundboard than an audience tape, but quality is poor, with heavy crowd noise and the band close in the mix; Recording quality is mediocre and the pitch runs slightly fast; Fair quality, somewhat warbly and a bit fast [5][6][7]
- **gd1981-04-25.157604.bear.gems.flac1648**: source not stated; 9 songs; 40 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1981-04-25.157603.bear.gems.flac2496**: source not stated; 9 songs; 40 min [4]

## Around the show

- The band seemed to be in very good spirits and played well [7]
- Lineup is Jerry, Bobby, Billy and John Kahn, so it isn't really the full Grateful Dead [8]
- Show was at Berkeley Community Theatre; the Garcia Band played The Stone later the same day [12]
- Attendee remembers the Berkeley Community Theatre as a nice small venue, with Garcia Band the same evening [14]
- Sing Out For Sight benefit with Garcia, Weir, Kruetzman, Hart and Kahn [1]
- Acoustic benefit set; encores were Oh Boy and a drums segment [2]
- Rosalie Sorrels and Kate Wolf opened the SEVA Sing Out for Sight benefit [3]
- Last known time Bear mixed front of house for Garcia [3]
- Sounds like the Garcia and Kahn shows of the same period; Kahn suits acoustic better than Phil [8]
- With Kahn instead of Phil, it differs from the usual Grateful Dead acoustic sound, but works well [10]
- Deep Elem Blues, Babe It Ain't No Lie, El Paso and Oh Boy were relatively rare acoustic choices for then [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-04-25.sbd.gems.103640.flac16**: transferred by Jamie Waddell; source: master cass > cass [1]
- **gd81-04-25.aud.munder.9728.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [2]
- **gd1981-04-25.157604.bear.gems.flac1648**: taped by Recorded by Augustus Owsley Stanley III (aka Bear) via Jamie Waddell; transferred by Transferred and mastered by Jim Blackwood Speed/pitch adjustment by Jason Chastain Minor repairs, track, FLAC, and pack by Steve Gravel; source: TDK MA90 cassette [3]
- **gd1981-04-25.157603.bear.gems.flac2496**: taped by Recorded by Augustus Owsley Stanley III (aka Bear) via Jamie Waddell; transferred by Transferred and mastered by Jim Blackwood Speed/pitch adjustment by Jason Chastain Minor repairs, track, FLAC, and pack by Steve Gravel; source: TDK MA90 cassette [4]
